title: API Reference
markdown:
The FastAPI surface lives in `openexecutive.api.main`, which mounts one router per topic. A shared-secret middleware gates every request via an `x-api-key` header, except `/health` and the `/webhook/*` callbacks (which carry their own verification). CORS is restricted to configured UI origins.

Endpoints grouped by router:

| Router | Key endpoints | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `POST /chat` | SSE stream of a live Executive turn. A `session_id` in the body must be the caller's own chat (owner or principal); any other id starts a fresh chat instead of writing into someone else's, and an unknown channel-namespaced id (contains `:`) is ignored so a web caller cannot squat an id a channel adapter will use. The request body optionally carries `page_context` (route, page title, guide section id, and a form descriptor with current values) — sent only by the Ask OE side panel so the Executive can explain the current page or propose form values. When the Executive calls its `propose_form_values` tool, the stream emits a `form_patch` event (`{type, form_id, fields, rationale, iteration}`) that the panel applies into the on-screen form as highlighted suggestions; the user reviews and saves through the form's normal submit path. |
| `sessions` | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}`, `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`, `DELETE /sessions/{id}` | List, read and delete saved chat sessions. Every per-session route is limited to the session's owner or the principal (a legacy ownerless session is the principal's alone); anyone else gets the same 404 as an unknown id. `DELETE` also drops the in-memory session. |
| `today` | `GET /today`, `GET /today/activity`, `GET /today/activity/daily` | Morning-brief aggregation, recent-action rail, and Pulse heartbeat heatmap (per-day activity counts). A decision proposal's alert and its resolved-activity row are shown only to the principal and the routed approver. |
| `people` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH /people`, `POST /people/{id}/archive` | Roster CRUD and scope lookups. Reads are open to signed-in users; adding, editing and archiving people are the principal's alone (anyone while no principal exists yet, so first setup works), including a person editing their own row. Anyone else gets 403 before any lookup. The Executive's roster tools are gated the same way, and so are the routes that wipe or swap the company's data (`/fixtures` and `/clients` writes) and the department-head field of `PATCH /departments/{slug}`, since a reset would otherwise let a teammate empty the roster and claim principal. Starting a workflow that writes the roster (`new_hire_onboarding`) and answering the setup wizard (`POST /onboard/answer`) are the owner's too. |
| `departments` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /departments`, `.../goals` | Department state and per-department goals. |
| `talent` | `GET|POST|PATCH /engagements`, `GET|POST|PATCH /candidates`, `POST /candidates/{id}/stage`, `GET /engagements/{id}/matches`, `GET /candidates/{id}/similar`, `POST /talent/reindex`, `GET|POST|PATCH /offers`, `POST /offers/{id}/{extend,decision,archive}` | Executive-search pipeline: searches, candidates, semantic matching, and the offer lifecycle (extend/decision return the offer plus approval state, scheduled/cancelled expiry nudges, side effects, and warnings; lifecycle conflicts are 409s). |
| `agents` | `GET /agents`, `PATCH /agents/{id}`, `POST /agents/{id}/test` | Specialist metadata and Council overrides. |
| `personas` | `GET\|PUT\|POST\|DELETE /personas` | Executive persona definitions. |
| `alerts` | `POST /alerts/{id}/ack` | Ack a briefing proposal (`read`/`ack`/`dismissed`) to groom the queue. A decision proposal's alert can be acked only by the principal or the routed approver (404 otherwise). The ingestion → triage → storage pipeline is unchanged, but alerts now surface only through the briefing (`/today` reads them directly) — there is no list, prefs, mutes, feedback, or live-stream endpoint. |
| `artifacts` | `GET /artifacts`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/archive` | Browsable research/document artifacts. |
| `decisions` | `GET /decisions`, `POST /decisions/{id}/{approve,reject,cancel}`, `GET /audit/reliability` | Approval-gated decision instances (e.g. calendar bookings). A decision is visible to the principal and its routed approver only (others get 404; the list is filtered; `/audit/reliability` is principal-only). A proposed booking is surfaced on the briefing as a companion alert; approve/reject/cancel here also clear that alert. Reviewed in the briefing — there is no separate proposals page. |
| `audit` | `GET /audit/logs`, `GET /audit/logs/{id}`, `GET /audit/sessions/{id}`, `GET /audit/usage`, `POST /audit/log` | Durable audit trail of side effects. `POST /audit/log` is server-only (the sign-in hook): requests carrying `x-caller-email` get 403 and fields are size-capped. `/audit/sessions/{id}` adds a per-session token cost summary; `/audit/usage` aggregates token usage and OpenRouter cost across all sessions (totals, by day, by model). |
| `architecture` | `GET /architecture/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | This documentation surface. |
| `guide` | `GET /guide/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | Plain-language user-guide content surface — mirrors `architecture` (static, version-controlled files; no LLM on the serving path). |
| `health` | `GET /health`, `GET /health/honcho` | Liveness probes (unauthenticated). |
| `documents` | `POST\|GET\|DELETE /documents`, `GET /documents/{filename}` | Upload, list, view extracted text, and delete indexed company docs. |
| `scheduled` | `GET\|DELETE` scheduled actions (`?status=…&order=asc\|desc`) | Pending and fired scheduled actions; `order` flips the `run_at` sort (asc=soonest-first for the upcoming queue, desc=most-recent-first for terminal-status history). |
| `watchlist` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /watchlist` | External-monitoring watchlist + signals. |
| `workflows` | `GET /workflows`, `POST /workflows/{name}/runs`, `GET\|POST\|PUT\|DELETE /workflows/custom` | Workflow catalog, run management, and user-created (dynamic) workflow CRUD. |
| `knowledge` | `/knowledge/builtin`, `/failures`, `/external`, `/search`, `/attachments` | MBA knowledge base and external sources. Documents created or edited through `/builtin` and `/failures` are saved to a writable overlay on the persistent volume (`BUILTIN_OVERLAY_PATH`), shipped files are never modified (an edit is an overlay copy, a delete of a shipped doc is a tombstone), a request body over about 6 MB is refused (413) before it is read, a document must be non-blank and at most 500,000 characters (422 otherwise) and the overlay at `BUILTIN_OVERLAY_MAX_BYTES` (413), and the list endpoints report each file's `origin` (`shipped`, `custom` or `edited`). |
| `skills` | `/skills`, `/skills/search` | Skill registry CRUD and search. |
| `evals` | `/evals/scenarios`, `/evals/runs` | Eval scenarios and run results. |
| `memories` | `/memories/{decisions,initiatives,advice}` | Episodic-memory record management. |
| `review` | `/review/items`, `/review/stats` | Knowledge review queue and annotations. |
| `onboarding` | `/onboard/start`, `/onboard/answer` | Company-profile setup wizard. |
| `company-profile` | `GET\|PATCH /company-profile` | Structured company profile. |
| `auth` | `GET /auth/allowed-emails` | Allowed sign-in emails. |
| `fixtures` | `/fixtures`, `/fixtures/{name}/load` | Demo-company fixture load/reset/snapshot. |
| `clients` | `/clients`, `/clients/generate`, `/clients/cockpit`, `/clients/save`, `/clients/{slug}/activate` | Client-company slots — multi-client mode for fractional use; create from current/blank/AI-generated intake draft (pasted notes and/or file attachments, multipart on `/clients/generate`), save-back switching, engagement metadata (PATCH), cross-client cockpit, delete. See the Client Companies section. |
| webhooks | `POST /webhook/telegram`, `POST /webhook/google-chat` | Inbound integration callbacks (self-verified). |
| MCP server | `POST\|GET /mcp` | Open Executive exposed as an MCP server (Streamable-HTTP). Not a router — a mounted FastMCP sub-app. Same shared-secret gate (`x-api-key`); exposes company context as resources and the specialist council as tools. See the MCP Server section. |
